$2 \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_2 \downarrow \frac{\text{ Quickly }}{\text{ decomposes }} 2 \mathrm{CuCN} \downarrow+(\mathrm{CN})_2 \uparrow$
$\mathrm{CuCN} \downarrow+3 \mathrm{CN}^{-} \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{3-}$
This complex is so stable (i.e., $\left[\mathrm{Cu}^{+}\right]$is too low) that $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ cannot precipitate $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{I})$ sulphide $\left(\mathrm{Cu}_2 \mathrm{~S}\right)$

6151.text: The normal to the curve $x=a(1+\cos \theta)$, $y=a \sin \theta$ at $\theta$ always passes through a fixed point, then the fixed point is
6151.sol:
Given, $x=a(1+\cos \theta)
\begin{aligned} \text{$ and $} y=a \sin \theta\\ \text{ and } \frac{d x}{d \theta}= a(-\sin \theta)\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d \theta}= a \cos \theta \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x}{d y}=-\tan \theta\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \frac{-d x}{d y}=\tan \theta \quad, \left[\therefore \text{ Slope of normal }=\frac{-1}{d y / d x}\right]\\ \text{ and } \end{aligned} Slope of normal$=\tan $\theta
Equation$ of $normal is \begin{aligned}
& y-a \sin \theta=\tan \theta(x-a-a \cos \theta)\\
& \Rightarrow y-a \sin \theta=x \tan \theta-a \tan \theta-a \sin \theta\\
& \Rightarrow y=\tan \theta(x-a)
\end{aligned} \therefore$ The line passes through the point $(a, 0)$.

6468.sol:
Given:

$\dfrac{13x + 43}{2x^{2} + 17x + 30} = \dfrac{A}{2x + 5} + \dfrac{B}{x + 6}$

$⇒ \dfrac{13x + 43}{2x^{2} + 17x + 30} = \dfrac{A\left(x + 6\right) + B\left(2x + 5\right)}{\left(2x + 5\right)\left(x + 6\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{13x + 43}{2x^{2} + 17x + 30} = \dfrac{\left(A + 2B\right)x + 6A + 5B}{2x^{2} + 17x + 30}$

$⇒ \left( A + 2B\right)x + 6A + 5B = 13x + 43$

On comparing, we get

A + 2B = 13 . . . . $\left( i\right)$

6A + 5B = 43 . . . . $\left(ii\right)$

On solving $\left(i\right)$ & $\left(ii\right)$, we get

$7B = 35 ⇒ B = 5$

A = 13 - 2B = 3$

So,

A^{2} + B^{2} = 9 + 25 = 34$

$\int \frac{d x}{1+\sin x}=\tan \left(\frac{x}{2}-\theta\right)+c \begin{aligned}& \text{ Now, } \int \frac{d x}{1+\sin x}=\int \frac{1-\sin x}{1-\sin ^2 x}d x+c \\

Given, \(\tan ^{-1}$\left[\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\cos x}{1+e^x}$d x\right]\)
Let \(I=\int_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} $\frac{\cos x}{1+e^x}$d x\)...(i)

& {$\left[\because \int_$a^b f(x) d x=\int_a^b f(a+b-x) d x\right]} \\
& =\int_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} $\frac{\cos x}{1+e^{-x}}$d x=\int_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} $\frac{e^x \cos x}{1+e^x}$d x \quad \ldots (ii)

Adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\$(\begin{gathered}$2 I=\int_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} $\frac{\left(e^x+1\right) \cos x}{\left(1+e^x\right)}$d x \quad \ldots (iii) \\
=\int_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} \cos x d x=[\sin x]_{-$\frac{\pi}{2}$}^{$\frac{\pi}{2}$} \\
\Rightarrow 2 I=[1+1]=2 \Rightarrow I=1 \\
\therefore \tan ^{-1}$\left[\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\cos x}{1+e^x}$d x\right]=\tan ^{-1}(1)=\tan ^{-1}$\left(\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}

$$

& \sec (\alpha+\beta)=\sqrt{1+\frac{p^2}{(q-1)^2}} \\

& =\frac{(q-1)^2}{(q-1)^2+p^2}\left[\frac{p^2+p^2(q-1)+q(q-1)^2}{(q-1)^2}\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

16731.text: Match of the following. Column IColumn IIA. Ratio of $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta U}$ in an isobaricprocess1. $\frac{T_1}{\left(T_1-T_2\right)}$B. Ratio of $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta W}$ in an isobaricprocess2. $\frac{T_2}{\left(T_1-T_2\right)}$C. Coefficient of performanceof a refrigerator3. $\frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}$D. Coefficient of performanceof a heat pump4. $\gamma$ Codes $\begin{array}{llll} A & B & C & D\end{array}$
16731.sol: We know that, at constant volume, Heat supplied, $\Delta Q_1=\Delta U=C_V \Delta T$ At constant pressure, heat supplied, $\Delta Q=C_p \Delta T=\Delta U+\Delta W$ Ratio of heat capacity at constant pressure to constant volume is $\gamma=\frac{C_p}{C_V}$ Now, $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta U}=\frac{C_p \Delta T}{C_V \Delta T}=\frac{C_p}{C_V}=\gamma$ Now, $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta W}=\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta Q-\Delta U}=\frac{C_p \Delta T}{C_p \Delta T-C_V \Delta T}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{C_p}{C_p-C_V}=\frac{C_p}{C_V\left(\frac{C_p}{C_V}-1\right)} \\ & =\frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1} \end{aligned}$ For refrigerator, coefficient of performance, $\begin{aligned} \beta & =\frac{Q_2}{W}=\frac{\text{ Heat absorbed from food stuff }}{\text{ Electrical work done }} \\ \therefore \quad \beta & =\frac{Q_2}{Q_1-Q_2} \end{aligned}$ Coefficient of heat pump $=\frac{\text{ Heat released }}{\text{ Electrical work }}$ i.e. $\quad \alpha=\frac{Q_1}{W}=\frac{Q_1}{Q_1-Q_2}$ We know that, $\frac{Q_1}{Q_2}=\frac{T_1}{T_2}$ So, we get, $\beta=\frac{Q_2}{Q_1-Q_2}=\frac{\frac{Q_2}{Q_1}}{1-\frac{Q_2}{Q_1}}=\frac{\frac{T_2}{T_1}}{1-\frac{T_2}{T_1}}=\frac{T_2}{T_1-T_2}$ and $\alpha=\frac{Q_1}{Q_1-Q_2}=\frac{\frac{Q_1}{Q_2}}{\frac{Q_1}{Q_2}-1}=\frac{\frac{T_1}{T_2}}{\frac{T_1}{T_2}-1}=\frac{T_1}{T_1-T_2}$ Hence, we get the best match as given by $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow 4, \mathrm{ B} \rightarrow 3, \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 2$ and $\mathrm{D} \rightarrow 1$.

19538.text: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Acetone undergoes reaction in presence of Ba(OH)_2$ on heating to form 4–Methylpent–3–en–2–one$

19538.sol:
Acetone (C$H_3$ COCH_3$) undergoes aldol condensation in the presence of a base like Ba(OH)_2$. Two molecules of acetone condense to form diacetone alcohol, which upon heating loses a water molecule to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone. \\ \\ 2 CH_3$ COCH_3\xrightarrow{\text{Ba(OH)}_2}$ (CH_3$)_2$ C(OH)CH_2$ COCH_3\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ (CH_3$)_2$ C=CHCOCH_3$ + H_2$ O \\ \\ The IUPAC name of the product (CH_3$)_2$ C=CHCOCH_3$ is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (commonly known as mesityl oxide). Thus, statement (A) is correct.

For the other options:
Statement (B) is incorrect because acetophenone (PhCOCH_3$) can be prepared by the reaction of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) with dimethyl cadmium ((CH_3$)_2$ Cd). \\ \\ Statement (C) is incorrect because acetophenone contains a methyl ketone group ($-$COCH_3$) and gives a positive iodoform test with I_2$ and a base (like Na_2$ CO_3$), forming a yellow precipitate of CHI_3$.

Statement (D) is incorrect because the Wolff-Kishner reduction (NH_2$ NH_2$ / KOH in glycol) of acetone (a 3-carbon compound) yields propane, not butane.

19959.sol:
Metallic character increases down a group and decreases from left to right across a period.

Potassium (K$) is an alkali metal in group 1 and period 4, making it the most metallic among the given elements. Boron (B$) is a metalloid in group 13 and period 2, making it the least metallic.

Magnesium (Mg$) and Aluminum (Al$) belong to period 3. Since $Mg$ is in group 2 and $Al$ is in group 13, $Mg$ is more metallic than $Al$.

The correct order of metallic character is $K > Mg > Al > B$.

The given order $Al > Mg > B > K$ is incorrect.

Answer: Metallic character - $Al > Mg > B > K$

20343.text: Identify the product [D] formed when Reactant [A] $(M M 78 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol})$ undergoes the series of reactions shown
20343.sol:
The reactant [A] has a molar mass of $78$ g/mol, which corresponds to benzene (C_6H_6$).

In the first step, benzene reacts with methyl chloride (MeCl$) in the presence of a catalyst (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to form toluene (C_7H_8$).

In the second step, toluene reacts with 3$ moles of $Cl_2$ at $385$ K. This is a free-radical side-chain chlorination reaction, which replaces the three hydrogen atoms of the methyl group with chlorine atoms, yielding benzotrichloride (C_6H_5CCl_3$) as product [C].

In the final step, benzotrichloride reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH_{(aq)}$). The three chlorine atoms are replaced by hydroxyl groups to form a gem-triol intermediate (C_6H_5C(OH)_3$), which is unstable and loses a water molecule to form benzoic acid (C_6H_5COOH$) as product [D].

Answer: Benzoic acid

20984.text: The slant height of a cone is fixed at $7 \mathrm{~cm}$. If the rate of increase of its height is $0.3 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$, then the rate of increase of its volume when its height is $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ is
20984.sol:
We have, slant height of cone $(l)=7 \mathrm{~cm}$
$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & l^{2}=h^{2}+r^{2} \quad \text{...(i)} \\
\Rightarrow & r^{2}=7^{2}-4^{2} \quad \text{[when h=4 cm]} \\
\Rightarrow & r^{2}=33 \\
\Rightarrow & r=\sqrt{33} \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}
$$
Now, differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t. $l$, we get
$$
\begin{gathered}
\quad 0=2 h \frac{d h}{d t}+2 r \frac{d r}{d t} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d r}{d t}=-\frac{h}{r} \frac{d h}{d t} \quad \text{...(ii)}  \\
\text { Volume of the cone, } V=\frac{1}{3} \pi r^{2} h \\
\frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[2 r h \frac{d r}{d t}+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[2 r h\left(\frac{-h}{r} \frac{d h}{d t}\right)+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right](\text { from Eq. (ii)) } \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[-2 h^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi \frac{d h}{d t}\left[-2 h^{2}+r^{2}\right] \\
\left.\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}\right]_{h=4} \quad=\frac{1}{3} \pi(0.3)\left[-2 \times 4^{2}+(\sqrt{33})^{2}\right] \\
\quad=\frac{\pi}{10}[1]=\frac{\pi}{10} \mathrm{cc} / \mathrm{sec}
\end{gathered}
$$

23148.subject: Physics
23148.text: A raft of density $600 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{m}^3$ and mass $120 \mathrm{ kg}$ floats in water. How much weight can be put on the raft to make it just sink?
23148.sol:
The density of the raft is $\rho_{r} = 600 \text{ kg/m}^3$. The mass of the raft is $M = 120 \text{ kg}$.

The volume of the raft is $V = \dfrac{M}{\rho_{r}} = \dfrac{120}{600} = 0.2 \text{ m}^3$.

For the raft to just sink in water (density $\rho_{w} = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$), the total weight of the raft and the added mass $m$ must be equal to the buoyant force acting on the raft when it is fully submerged.

The buoyant force is $F_{B} = V \rho_{w} g = 0.2 \times 1000 \times g = 200g$.

The total weight is $(M + m)g = (120 + m)g$.

Equating the two, we have $120 + m = 200$.

Therefore, $m = 200 - 120 = 80 \text{ kg}$.

25482.text: A solution curve of differential equation $\left({x}^{2} + xy + 4x + 2y + 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - {y}^{2} = 0, x > 0$ passes through the point (1, 3). Then the solution curve -
options: Intersects $y = x + 2$ exactly at one point
Intersects  $y = x + 2$  exactly at two points
25482.sol:
$\left({x}^{2} + xy + 4x + 2y + 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - {y}^{2} = 0$
⇒$\left({\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + y\left(x + 2\right)\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = {y}^{2}$
Let $x + 2 = X, y = Y$
⇒$\left(X\right)\left(X + Y\right)\dfrac{dY}{dX} = {Y}^{2}$
⇒$- {X}^{2}dY = XYdY - {Y}^{2}dX$
⇒$- {X}^{2}dY = Y\left(XdY - YdX\right)$
⇒$- \dfrac{dY}{Y} = \dfrac{XdY - YdX}{{X}^{2}}$
Integrate both sides
⇒ $- ln\left|Y\right| = \left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right) + C$
Putting back X, Y in x, y terms
⇒$- ln\left|y\right| = \dfrac{y}{x + 2} + C$
$∵$ it is passing through (1, 3) , $- ln3 = 1 + C$
$C = - 1 - ln3$
$∴$ curve equation is $\dfrac{y}{x + 2} + ln\left|y\right| - 1 - ln3 = 0, x > 0$ .....(i)
Put $y = x + 2$ in equation (i)
then $\dfrac{x + 2}{x + 2} + ln\left|x + 2\right| - 1 - ln3 = 0$
$x = 1, - 5$ (reject as given $x > 0$ )
$∴$ curve intersect $y = x + 2$ at point (1, 3),(Only one point); put $y = {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2}$ , we will get $x + 2 + 2ln\left(x + 2\right) = 1 + ln3$
Clearly left hand side is an increasing function. Hence, it is always greater than $2 + 2ln2$ (By Putting X = 0)
Therefore no solution $y = {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2}$ put $y = {\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}$ in equation (i)
$\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{x + 2} + ln{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2} - 1 - ln3 = 0$
$\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{x + 2} + ln\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{3} - 1 = 0$
$∵ x > 0 ⇒ x + 3 > x + 2 and x + 3 > 3$
So $\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{x + 2} + ln\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{3} > 1$
$∴ \dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{x + 2} + ln\dfrac{{\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}}{3} - 1 = 0$ has no solution
$⇒$ curve $y = {\left(x + 3\right)}^{2}$ does not intersect

25856.subject: Mathematics
25856.text:
In a study about a pandemic, data of $900$ persons was collected. It was found that

$190$ persons had symptom of fever,

$220$ persons had symptom of cough,

$220$ persons had symptom of breathing problem,

$330$ persons had symptom of fever or cough or both,

$350$ persons had symptom of cough or breathing problem or both,

$340$ persons had symptom of fever or breathing problem or both,

$30$ persons had all three symptoms (fever, cough and breathing problem).

If a person is chosen randomly from these $900$ persons, then the probability that the person has at most one symptom is ______.
25856.sol:
We denote the set of people having symptoms of fever, cough and breathing problem by $F, C$ and $B$ respectively

Given that $n\left(F\right) = 190, n\left(B\right) = 220$ and $n\left(C\right) = 220$

Also given, $n\left(F ∪ C\right) = 330, n\left(B ∪ C\right) = 350,$ $n\left(F ∪ B\right) = 340$ and $n\left(F ∩ C ∩ B\right) = 30$

So $n\left(F ∩ C\right) = n\left(F\right) + n\left(C\right) - n\left(F ∪ C\right)$

$= 80$

Similarly, $n\left(F ∩ B\right) = n\left(F\right) + n\left(B\right) - n\left(F ∪ B\right) = 70$ and $n\left(C ∩ B\right) = n\left(C\right) + n\left(B\right) - n\left(B ∪ C\right) = 90$

Putting the data in Venn diagram

Number of people having at most one symptom$=$Number of people having zero symptom or one symptom

$= 70 + 80 + 90 + 480 = 720$

Required probability $= \dfrac{720}{900} = 0 . 8$

27026.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
ReagentsReaction Name (Involving aldehydes)
A. H_{2}, Pd-BaSO_{4}I. Etard Reaction
B. SnCl_{2}, HClII. Rosenmund Reduction
C. CrO_{2} Cl_{2}, CS_{2}III. Gatterman - Koch Reaction
D. CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl_{3}IV. Stephen Reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
27026.sol:
Matching reagents with aldehyde reaction types:

A (H2, Pd-BaSO4) is the Lindlar/Rosenmund catalyst used in Rosenmund Reduction to convert acyl chlorides to aldehydes, matching with II.

B (SnCl2, HCl) is used in Stephen Reaction where nitriles are converted to aldehydes via imine intermediate, matching with IV.

C (CrO2Cl2, CS2) is Jones-like reagent used in Etard Reaction for oxidizing methyl groups on aromatic rings to aldehydes, matching with I.

D (CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl3) is the Gatterman-Koch Reaction which directly converts benzene to benzaldehyde using CO and AlCl3 catalyst, matching with III.

Therefore the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

Consider the following sequence of reactions.

Assuming that the reaction proceeds to completion, then 137 mg of 4 -nitrotoluene will produce $\_\_\_\_$ mg of $B$. (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{H}: 1, \mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{~N}: 14, \mathrm{O}: 16, \mathrm{Br}: 80$)
27203.sol:
Starting with 137 mg of 4-nitrotoluene (C₇H₉NO₂, MW = 137).
Step 1: Reduction with Sn/HCl converts NO₂ to NH₂, producing 4-aminotoluene (A).
Step 2: Acetylation with (CH₃CO)₂O produces the acetamide intermediate, then bromination with Br₂/AcOH adds bromine to the para position (ortho-para directing due to acetamide group), yielding 4-bromo-N-(4-methylphenyl)acetamide (B) with molecular formula C₉H₁₀BrNO and MW = 228 g/mol.
Moles of starting material = 137 mg ÷ 137 g/mol = 1 mmol.
Assuming complete reaction, moles of B produced = 1 mmol.
Mass of B = 1 mmol × 228 mg/mmol = 228 mg.

At $298K$, the equilibrium constant is $2 \times {10}^{15}$ for the reaction:

$Cu\left(s\right) + 2{Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right) ⇌ {Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + 2Ag\left(s\right)$

The equilibrium constant for the reaction

$\dfrac{1}{2}{Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + Ag\left(s\right) ⇌ \dfrac{1}{2}Cu\left(s\right) + {Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right)$ is $x \times {10}^{- 8}$. The value of $x$ is ______. (Round off the answer to the nearest integer)
28054.sol:
$Cu\left(s\right) + 2{Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right) ⇌ {Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + 2Ag\left(s\right); {K}_{eq} = 2 \times {10}^{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}{Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + Ag\left(s\right) ⇌ \dfrac{1}{2}Cu\left(s\right) + {Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right)$

The equilibrium reaction is reversed and multiplied with $\dfrac{1}{2}$,

Hence, ${K}_{eq}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{K}_{eq}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2 \times {10}^{15}}} = x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{20}} \times \dfrac{1}{{10}^{7}} = x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{20}} \times {10}^{- 7} = x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{20}} = x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{5} = 2 . 236$

$≃ 2 . 24$

30396.subject: Chemistry
30396.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: $3$-phenylpropene reacts with HBr and gives secondary alkyl bromide having a chiral carbon atom as the major product.

Statement II: Aryl chlorides and aryl cyanides can be prepared by Sandmeyer reaction as well as Gattermann reaction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
30396.sol:
Statement I:
When $3$-phenylpropene reacts with $HBr$, protonation of the alkene occurs to form a secondary carbocation.

$C_6H_5-CH_2-CH=CH_2 + H^+ \rightarrow C_6H_5-CH_2-CH^+-CH_3$

This secondary carbocation undergoes a $1,2$-hydride shift to form a more stable, resonance-stabilized benzylic carbocation.

$C_6H_5-CH_2-CH^+-CH_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5-CH^+-CH_2-CH_3$

The bromide ion then attacks this benzylic carbocation to form the major product, $1$-bromo-$1$-phenylpropane.

$C_6H_5-CH^+-CH_2-CH_3 + Br^- \rightarrow C_6H_5-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_3$

The carbon atom bonded to the bromine is attached to four different groups: a phenyl group ($-C_6H_5$), an ethyl group ($-CH_2CH_3$), a hydrogen atom ($-H$), and a bromine atom ($-Br$). Thus, it is a chiral carbon. The product is a secondary alkyl bromide. Therefore, Statement I is true.

Statement II:
The Sandmeyer reaction involves treating a diazonium salt with $Cu(I)$ salts ($CuCl$, $CuBr$, $CuCN$) to prepare aryl chlorides, aryl bromides, and aryl cyanides, respectively.

The Gattermann reaction involves treating a diazonium salt with copper powder ($Cu$) and halogen acids ($HCl$, $HBr$) to prepare aryl chlorides and aryl bromides. Aryl cyanides are not prepared using the Gattermann reaction. Therefore, Statement II is false.

Conclusion: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

34584.text: If the system of equations $x + y + z = 5,$ $x + 2y + 3z = 9,$ $x + 3y + \alphaz = \beta$ has inifinitely many solutions, then $\beta - \alpha$ equals
34584.sol:
The system of linear equations ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z + {d}_{1} = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z + {d}_{2} = 0$ and ${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z + {d}_{3} = 0$ have infinitely many solutions, if

$D = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

and ${D}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

Hence, for the system of equations $x + y + z = 5, x + 2y + 3z = 9$ and $x + 3y + \alphaz = \beta$ have infinitely many solution, if

$D = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & \alpha\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(2\alpha - 9\right) - \left(\alpha - 3\right) + \left(3 - 2\right)$

$⇒ 2\alpha - 9 - \alpha + 3 + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = 5 .$

And, ${D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & 3 \\ \beta & 3 & \alpha\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & 3 \\ \beta & 3 & 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 5\left(10 - 9\right) - \left(45 - 3\beta\right) + \left(27 - 2\beta\right) = 0$

$⇒ 5 - 45 + 3\beta + 27 - 2\beta = 0$

$⇒ \beta = 13 .$

Hence, $\beta - \alpha = 13 - 5 = 8 .$

34639.text: If the curve $y = f(x)$ passes through the point $(1, e)$ and satisfies the differential equation $dy = y(2 + \log_e x)\,dx$, $x > 0$, then $f(e)$ is equal to :
34639.sol:
Given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{y} = (2 + \log_e x) dx$

Integrating both sides, we get:

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y} = \int (2 + \log_e x) dx$

$\log_e y = 2x + x \log_e x - x + C$

$\log_e y = x + x \log_e x + C$

Since the curve passes through $(1, e)$, substitute $x = 1$ and $y = e$:

$\log_e e = 1 + 1 \cdot \log_e 1 + C$

$1 = 1 + 0 + C \Rightarrow C = 0$

The equation of the curve is $\log_e y = x + x \log_e x$

To find $f(e)$, substitute $x = e$:

$\log_e y = e + e \log_e e$

$\log_e y = e + e(1) = 2e$

$y = e^{2e}$

Answer: $e^{2e}$

38118.text: Let the line $L$ be the projection of the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2}$ in the plane $x - 2y - z = 3$. If $d$ is the distance of the point $( 0, 0, 6 )$ from $L$, then ${d}^{2}$ is equal to
38118.sol:
Let

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2} = r$

Any point on the line $P\left(2r + 1, r + 3, 2r + 4\right)$

For the point $P\left(2r + 1, r + 3, 2r + 4\right)$ to lie on the plane, its co-ordinates should satisfy the equation $x - 2y - z = 3$.

$⇒ \left(2r + 1\right) - 2\left(r + 3\right) - \left(2r + 4\right) = 3$

$⇒ - 2r - 9 = 3$

$⇒ r = - 6$

$∴ P\left(- 11, - 3, - 8\right)$

Now, let $Q\left(h, k, l\right)$ be the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from$\left(1, 3, 4\right)$ to the plane $x - 2y - z = 3$.

$⇒ \dfrac{h - 1}{1} = \dfrac{k - 3}{- 2} = \dfrac{l - 4}{- 1} = \dfrac{- \left(1 - 6 - 4 - 3\right)}{1 + 4 + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{h - 1}{1} = \dfrac{k - 3}{- 2} = \dfrac{l - 4}{- 1} = 2$

$⇒ h = 3, k = - 1, l = 2$

$∴ Q\left(h, k, l\right) = Q\left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

Therefore, projection line $PQ$ is

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{3 - \left(- 11\right)} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1 - \left(- 3\right)} = \dfrac{z - 2}{2 - \left(- 8\right)}$

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{14} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{10}$

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{7} = \dfrac{y + 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5}$

Let, $L: \dfrac{x - 3}{7} = \dfrac{y + 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5} = \lambda \ldots \left(i\right)$

Direction ratio of $AC$ are $\left(7\lambda + 3, \lambda - 1, 5\lambda - 4\right)$

Now, $AC$ is perpendicular to the projection line $( i )$ So,

$7\left(7\lambda + 3\right) + \left(\lambda - 1\right) + 5\left(5\lambda - 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ 49\lambda + 21 + \lambda - 1 + 25\lambda - 20 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 0$

So,

$∴ C ≡ \left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

Now,

${d}^{2} = {3}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 6\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {d}^{2} = 26$

42953.text: The critical angle for a denser-rarer interface is $45 °$. The speed of light in rarer medium is $3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}$. The speed of light in the denser medium is:
42953.sol:
The critical angle and the refractive index of a media are related by the formula:

$sin{\theta}_{c} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the value of the critical angle into equation (1) and solve to calculate the refractive index of the medium.

$\begin{cases}sin45 ° & = & \dfrac{1}{\mu} \\ ⇒ & \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\mu} \\ ⇒ & \mu = \sqrt{2}\end{cases}$

The refractive index of the medium can also be written as

$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) and solve to calculate the required speed of light within the medium.

$\begin{cases}\sqrt{2} & = & \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}}{v} \\ ⇒ & v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}}{\sqrt{2}} \\ = & 2 . 12 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}\end{cases}$

43725.sol:
According to the Newton's law of cooling, $- \dfrac{dT}{dt} = K\left(T - {T}_{0}\right)$.

Applying approximation, $- \dfrac{∆ T}{∆ t} = K\left(\dfrac{{T}_{1} + {T}_{2}}{2} - {T}_{0}\right)$

For first $6min$, ${T}_{1} = 80 ° C, {T}_{2} = \left(40 + 20\right) = 60 ° C, {T}_{0} = 20 ° C$

$⇒ - \dfrac{\left(60 - 80\right)}{6} = K\left(70 - 20\right) ⇒ K = - \dfrac{\left(60 - 80\right)}{6 \times \left(70 - 20\right)}$

$⇒ K = \dfrac{20}{6 \times 50} = \dfrac{1}{15}$

For $6\text{to}{t}_{2}$, ${T}_{1} = 60 ° C, {T}_{2} = \left(20 + 20\right) = 40 ° C, {T}_{0} = 20 ° C$

$- \dfrac{\left(60 - 80\right)}{\left({t}_{2} - 6\right)} = K\left(50 - 20\right) ⇒ {t}_{2} - 6 = 15 \times \dfrac{20}{30} ⇒ {t}_{2} = 16min$

50652.text: A wafer of pure germanium crystal has two parts X and Y. The end X is obtained by doping with arsenic and Y with indium. It is connected to a battery as shown in the figure. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: X is p-type, Y is n-type and the junction is forward biased
X is n-type, Y is p-type and the junction is forward biased
X is p-type, Y is n-type and the junction is reverse biased
X is n-type, Y is p-type and the junction is reverse biased
50652.sol:
Part X of the germanium crystal is doped with arsenic. Arsenic is a Group 15 (pentavalent) element, so doping with it provides extra electrons, making X an n-type semiconductor.

Part Y is doped with indium. Indium is a Group 13 (trivalent) element, which creates holes, making Y a p-type semiconductor.

In the given circuit diagram, the battery symbol has a longer line on the left and a shorter, thicker line on the right. This means the left side is the positive terminal and the right side is the negative terminal.

Since part X (n-type) is connected to the positive terminal and part Y (p-type) is connected to the negative terminal, the p-n junction is reverse biased.

Therefore, X is n-type, Y is p-type, and the junction is reverse biased.

Answer: X is n-type, Y is p-type and the junction is reverse biased

53272.text: What are the values of $c$ for which Rolle's theorem for the function $f(x)=x^3-3 x^2+2 x$ in the interval $[0,2]$ is verified?
53272.sol:
Here, we observe that (a) $f(x)$ is a polynomial, so it is continuous in the interval $[0,2]$. (b) $f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2-6 x+2$ exists for all $x \in(0,2)$.
So, $f(x)$ is differentiable for all $x \in(0,2)$ and (c) $f(0)=0, f(2)=2^3-3(2)^2+2(2)=0\Rightarrow f(0)=f(2)$
Thus, all the three conditions of Rolle's theorem are satisfied.
So, there must exist $c \in[0,2]$ such that $f^{\prime}(c)=0\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & f^{\prime}(c)=3 c^2-6 c+2=0 \\ \Rightarrow & c=1 \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \in[0,2] \end{array}$

55483.text: Which carbon atom of glucopyranose numbered from $\mathrm{C}-1$ to $\mathrm{C}-6$ is anomeric?
55483.sol:
The anomeric carbon in cyclic sugars originates from the carbonyl carbon in the open-chain form. In glucose, an aldohexose, the aldehyde group is located at $\mathrm{C}-1$.

During cyclization to form glucopyranose, the $\mathrm{C}-1$ aldehyde carbon reacts with the hydroxyl group at $\mathrm{C}-5$, forming a hemiacetal. This positions $\mathrm{C}-1$ as bonded to both the ring oxygen and the anomeric hydroxyl group.

$\mathrm{C}-1$ becomes chiral upon ring formation and serves as the anomeric carbon.

The correct identification is $\mathrm{D}$.

57976.sol:
Strong electrolytes dissociate completely in an aqueous solution.

$\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{KOH}$ are strong bases and dissociate completely into their respective ions.

$\text{HI}$ is a strong acid and also dissociates completely into ions.

$\text{NH}_3$ is a weak base and dissociates only partially in an aqueous solution to form $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ ions.

Thus, $\text{NH}_3$ is a weak electrolyte.

58616.text: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in $\text{KO}_2$ ?
58616.sol:
Let the oxidation number of oxygen in $\text{KO}_2$ be $x$.

Potassium is an alkali metal, so its oxidation state is always $+1$ in its compounds.

The sum of oxidation states of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

$+1 + 2x = 0$

$2x = -1$

$x = -1/2$

The oxidation number of oxygen in $\text{KO}_2$ is $-1/2$.

Answer: $-1/2$

Since fluorine has oxidation state $-1$ and the compound is neutral, the oxidation number $x$ of xenon satisfies:

$x + 6 \times (-1) = 0$

$x = +6$

61652.sol:
Using the trigonometric identity $\cos x \cos 2x \cos 2^2x \dots \cos 2^{n-1}x = \dfrac{\sin(2^n x)}{2^n \sin x}$

For $n=5$, the given function can be written as:

$f(x) = \dfrac{\sin(32x)}{32 \sin x}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the quotient rule:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{32 \sin x \cdot 32 \cos(32x) - \sin(32x) \cdot 32 \cos x}{(32 \sin x)^2}$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{32 \cos(32x) \sin x - \sin(32x) \cos x}{32 \sin^2 x}$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$32x = 32 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} = 8\pi$

Since $\cos(8\pi) = 1$ and $\sin(8\pi) = 0$, we get:

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{32(1)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - 0}{32 \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$

$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \text{cosec}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

Answer: $\text{cosec}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

63314.subject: Mathematics
63314.text: If the equation $16x^2 - 24xy + 9y^2 - 8x + 6y - 35 = 0$ represents a pair of straight lines, then the equation of the locus of points equidistant from these two lines is..........
63314.sol:
The given equation is $16x^2 - 24xy + 9y^2 - 8x + 6y - 35 = 0$.

This can be rewritten by grouping the terms as:

$(4x - 3y)^2 - 2(4x - 3y) - 35 = 0$

Let $t = 4x - 3y$. The equation becomes:

$t^2 - 2t - 35 = 0$

$(t - 7)(t + 5) = 0$

$t = 7$ or $t = -5$

Substituting back $t = 4x - 3y$, the equation represents two parallel straight lines:

$4x - 3y - 7 = 0$ and $4x - 3y + 5 = 0$

The locus of points equidistant from these two parallel lines is a line parallel to them and lying exactly midway between them. Its equation is given by the arithmetic mean of their constant terms:

$4x - 3y + \dfrac{-7 + 5}{2} = 0$

$4x - 3y - 1 = 0$

Answer: $4x - 3y - 1 = 0$

63455.subject: Mathematics
63455.text: Angle between the parabola $y^2=4(x-1)$ and $x^2+4(y-3)=0$ at the common end of their latus rectum is
63455.sol:
Determine the angle between the parabolas at their intersection point.

The parabolas are $y^2 = 4(x-1)$ and $x^2 = -4(y-3)$, with their latus rectum endpoints determined by their respective focus coordinates.

For the parabola $y^2 = 4(x-1)$, the vertex is $(1,0)$ and the focus is $(2,0)$, giving latus rectum ends at $(2,2)$ and $(2,-2)$.

For $x^2 = -4(y-3)$, the vertex is $(0,3)$ and the focus is $(0,2)$; ends of the latus rectum correspond to $x = \pm 2$, $y=2$, resulting in endpoints of $(2,2)$ and $(-2,2)$.

The common point is $(2,2)$.

Differentiating $y^2 = 4(x-1)$ implicitly gives $2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 4$, so $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2}{y}$. At $(2,2)$, the slope is $m_1 = 1$.

Differentiating $x^2 = -4(y-3)$ yields $2x = -4\frac{dy}{dx}$, so $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{2}$, giving $m_2 = -1$ at $(2,2)$.

The angle $\theta$ between the tangents follows from $\tan\theta = \left|\frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2}\right|$, and with $m_1 = 1$, $m_2 = -1$, the denominator is $1 - 1 = 0$, indicating perpendicular tangents and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

The angle between the parabolas at their common latus rectum end is $\frac{\pi}{2}$, corresponding to option A.

64366.subject: Mathematics
64366.text: If A and B are the feet of the perpendiculars drawn from $(1, 2, 3)$ to planes $YZ$ and $ZX$, then the equation of the plane passing through the points A, B and the origin is
64366.sol:
Let the given point be $P(1, 2, 3)$.

The foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to the $YZ$-plane (x = 0$) is $A(0, 2, 3)$.

The foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to the $ZX$-plane (y = 0$) is $B(1, 0, 3)$.

The equation of the plane passing through the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ is $ax + by + cz = 0$.

Since the plane passes through $A(0, 2, 3)$ and $B(1, 0, 3)$, we have:

$2b + 3c = 0$

$a + 3c = 0$

Solving these equations, we get $a = -3c$ and $b = -\dfrac{3}{2}c$.

Substituting the values of $a$ and $b$ in the equation of the plane:

$-3cx - \dfrac{3}{2}cy + cz = 0$

Dividing by $-\dfrac{c}{2}$, we get the required equation of the plane:

$6x + 3y - 2z = 0$

Answer: $6x + 3y - 2z = 0$

64438.text: If the lines $\frac{1-x}{2}=\frac{7 y+4}{2 \lambda}=\frac{2 z-5}{2}$ and $\frac{7-7 x}{3 \lambda}=\frac{y-1}{7}=\frac{6-z}{5}$ are at right angle, then the value of $\lambda$ is
64438.sol:
The condition for perpendicular lines requires that the dot product of their direction vectors is zero. For lines in the form $\frac{x-x_1}{a} = \frac{y-y_1}{b} = \frac{z-z_1}{c}$, the direction ratios are $(a, b, c)$.

Rewriting the first equation $\frac{1-x}{2} = \frac{7y+4}{2\lambda} = \frac{2z-5}{2}$ in standard form gives direction ratios $(-2, \frac{2\lambda}{7}, 1)$.

The second equation $\frac{7-7x}{3\lambda} = \frac{y-1}{7} = \frac{6-z}{5}$ yields direction ratios $(-\frac{3\lambda}{7}, 7, -5)$.

Setting the dot product to zero: $(-2)(-\frac{3\lambda}{7}) + (\frac{2\lambda}{7})(7) + (1)(-5) = 0$

Simplifying: $\frac{6\lambda}{7} + 2\lambda - 5 = 0$

Multiplying through by 7: $6\lambda + 14\lambda - 35 = 0$
$20\lambda = 35$
$\lambda = \frac{7}{4}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

64479.text: The direction cosines of the line $x-y+2 z=5$ and $3 x+y+z=6$ are
64479.sol:
Direction cosines of the line intersection are determined by the direction vector perpendicular to both plane normals. For planes $x - y + 2z = 5$ and $3x + y + z = 6$, normal vectors are $\mathrm{n_1} = \langle 1, -1, 2 \rangle$ and $\mathrm{n_2} = \langle 3, 1, 1 \rangle$.

The direction vector $\mathrm{d}$ is their cross product:
$\mathrm{d} = \mathrm{n_1} \times \mathrm{n_2} = \langle (-1)(1) - (2)(1), (2)(3) - (1)(1), (1)(1) - (-1)(3) \rangle = \langle -3, 5, 4 \rangle$

Its magnitude is $|\mathrm{d}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 5^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

The direction cosines are:
$l = \frac{-3}{5\sqrt{2}}$, $m = \frac{5}{5\sqrt{2}}$, $n = \frac{4}{5\sqrt{2}}$

These correspond to option A.

64756.text:
The direction cosines of a line which lies in ZoX plane and makes an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$
with Z-axis are
64756.sol:
Direction cosines are the cosines of the angles which a line makes with the positive coordinate axes in anticlockwise direction. They are represented by $\langle l, m, n\rangle$ where $\mathrm{l}, \mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n}$ correspond to the $\mathrm{x}$-axis, $\mathrm{y}$-axis, and $\mathrm{z}$-axis respectively. One important property of direction cosines is that the sum of their squares is unity.
i.e., $l^{2}+m^{2}+n^{2}=1$
If the line lies in the zox plane, it implies that the $y$-axis is normal to the line as the $y$-axis is normal to the ZOX plane. Which means the angle the line makes with the $y$-axis is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ or $\frac{\pi}{2}$ radians. Thus, $m=\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0$ It is given that the line makes an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ or $\frac{\pi}{6}$ radians with the positive z-axis. Thus, $n=\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
Now we use the property $l^{2}+m^{2}+n^{2}=1$
Substituting the values of $m$ and $n$, we get the following values of à¥¤ $l=\pm \frac{1}{2}$
We get two values of I because the only information given is that the line makes an angle of $\frac{\pi}{6}$ with the z-axis, so it can make an angle of either $\frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\frac{2 \pi}{3}$ with the $x$-axis, which correspond to the two values of I.
Therefore, the direction cosines are
$\langle l, m, n\rangle=\left\langle\pm \frac{1}{2}, 0, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right\rangle$

66990.text: A charge $Q$ is placed at each corner of a cube of side $r$. The potential at the centre of the cube is (\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)$
66990.sol:
The length of the body diagonal of a cube of side $r$ is $r\sqrt{3}$.

The distance from the centre of the cube to any corner is half of the body diagonal, which is $d = \dfrac{r\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

The electric potential at the centre due to a single charge $Q$ at one corner is $V_1 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{d}$.

Since there are $8$ identical charges at the $8$ corners, the total potential at the centre is $V = 8 V_1$.

Substituting the value of $d$:

$V = 8 \times \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{\dfrac{r\sqrt{3}}{2}}$

$V = \dfrac{16Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r\sqrt{3}}$

$V = \dfrac{4Q}{\pi\epsilon_0 r\sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4Q}{\pi\epsilon_0 r\sqrt{3}}$

66996.subject: Physics
66996.text:
An uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius 'R' has uniform surface charge density '$\sigma$'. It is made of two hemispherical identical shells held together by pressing them with force 'F' as shown. F is proportional to
[$\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space]
66996.sol:
The electrostatic pressure $P$ on the surface of a uniformly charged thin spherical shell is given by:

$P = \dfrac{\sigma^2}{2\epsilon_0}$

Consider a small area element $dA$ on the surface of one of the hemispheres. The outward electrostatic force on this element is:

$dF = P dA = \dfrac{\sigma^2}{2\epsilon_0} dA$

By symmetry, the net force on the hemisphere will be directed along the axis perpendicular to its circular base. The component of the force along this axis is:

$dF_{\perp} = dF \cos\theta = P dA \cos\theta$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the radially outward normal and the axis of symmetry.

Integrating this over the entire surface of the hemisphere gives the total repulsive force:

$F_{rep} = \int P dA \cos\theta = P \int dA \cos\theta$

The term $\int dA \cos\theta$ represents the projected area of the hemisphere onto the plane of its base, which is simply the area of a circle of radius $R$:

$\int dA \cos\theta = \pi R^2$

Substituting this back, we get the net repulsive force:

$F_{rep} = \left(\dfrac{\sigma^2}{2\epsilon_0}\right) (\pi R^2) = \dfrac{\pi \sigma^2 R^2}{2\epsilon_0}$

To hold the two hemispheres together, the external applied force $F$ must balance this electrostatic repulsion:

$F = \dfrac{\pi \sigma^2 R^2}{2\epsilon_0}$

From this expression, it is clear that the force $F$ is proportional to $\dfrac{\sigma^2 R^2}{\epsilon_0}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\epsilon_0}\,\sigma^2 R^2$

67226.text: The gravitational pull of the moon is $\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{\text{th }}$ of the earth and mass of moon is $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{\text{th }}$ of the earth. This implies that the
options: radius of moon is $(1 / 4)^{\text{th }}$ of the earth's radius.
radius of the earth is $(\sqrt{4 / 3})^{\text{th }}$ of the moon's radius.
moon's radius is half that of the earth.
radius of the earth is $(4 / 3)^{\text{th }}$ of the moon's radius.
67226.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a celestial body's surface is governed by $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, where $M$ is mass and $R$ is radius. Given that lunar gravity is one-sixth of Earth's, $g_m = \frac{1}{6} g_e$, and lunar mass is one-eighth of Earth's, $M_m = \frac{1}{8} M_e$.

Substituting into the gravity formula yields $\frac{GM_m}{R_m^2} = \frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{GM_e}{R_e^2}$. After canceling $G$ and $M_e$ using the mass relation, $\frac{1}{8R_m^2} = \frac{1}{6R_e^2}$.

Cross-multiplying gives $6R_e^2 = 8R_m^2$, simplifying to $3R_e^2 = 4R_m^2$. Solving for the radii, $R_e = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} R_m$, confirming that Earth's radius is $\sqrt{4/3}$ times the Moon's.

Only option B matches this result.

The total length of the wire in the coil is $l = N \times \text{perimeter of one turn}$, where $N$ is the number of turns.

Thus, the resistance of the galvanometer is directly proportional to the number of turns (R \propto N$).

When the number of turns in the coil decreases, the total length of the wire decreases.

Consequently, the resistance of the galvanometer decreases.

68119.subject: Physics
68119.text: Three liquids have same surface tension and densities $\rho_1$, $\rho_2$ and $\rho_3$ (\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$). In three identical capillaries rise of liquid is same. The corresponding angle of contact \theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\theta_3$ are related as
68119.sol:
The formula for capillary rise is $h = \dfrac{2T \cos\theta}{r \rho g}$.

Rearranging the formula, we get $\cos\theta = \dfrac{h r g}{2T} \rho$.

Since $h$, $r$, $g$, and $T$ are constant for all three liquids, $\cos\theta \propto \rho$.

Given that $\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$, it follows that $\cos\theta_1 < \cos\theta_2 < \cos\theta_3$.

For capillary rise, the angle of contact $\theta$ is acute (0 \le \theta < 90^{}^{\circ}$). In this interval, the cosine function is strictly decreasing.

Therefore, a smaller value of \cos\theta$ corresponds to a larger angle $\theta$, which gives $\theta_1 > \theta_2 > \theta_3$.

Answer: $\theta_1 > \theta_2 > \theta_3$

68158.subject: Physics
68158.text: A wind with speed $50 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ blows parallel to the roof of a house. The area of the roof is $300 \mathrm{ m}^2$. Assume that the pressure inside the house is atmospheric pressure. Density of air is $1.2 \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. The magnitude of the force exerted by the wind on the roof will be
68158.sol:
The force magnitude is determined by the pressure difference created by wind flow over the roof using Bernoulli's principle.

Applying Bernoulli's equation between a point just above the roof and inside the house, where height differences are negligible:

$P_1 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_2^2$

With $v_1 = 50\ \mathrm{m/s}$, $v_2 = 0\ \mathrm{m/s}$, and $\rho = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$:

$P_1 + \frac{1}{2}(1.2)(50)^2 = P_{\text{atm}} + 0$

$P_1 + 1500\ \mathrm{Pa} = P_{\text{atm}}$

The pressure difference is $\Delta P = P_{\text{atm}} - P_1 = 1500\ \mathrm{Pa}$.

Using $F = \Delta P \times A$ with $A = 300\ \mathrm{m^2}$:

$F = 1500 \times 300 = 450000\ \mathrm{N}$

The magnitude of the force is $4.5 \times 10^5\ \mathrm{N}$.

$\boxed{\text{C}}$

69021.text: The radii of curvature of both the surfaces of a convex lens of focal length ' $f$ ' and focal power ' $\mathrm{P}$ ' are equal. One of the surfaces is made plane by grinding. The new focal length and focal power of the lens is
69021.sol:
From Lens maker's formula,
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right)$
As the radius of both the surfaces is the same,
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{R}}(\mu-1)$
When one surface is plane, $R_1=R, R_2=\infty$
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}(\mu-1)$
$\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{f}}=2$
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime}=2 \mathrm{f}$
$P=\frac{1}{f} \quad$ and $\quad P^{\prime}=\frac{1}{f^{\prime}}$
$\frac{\mathrm{P}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{2}$
$\mathrm{P}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{P}}{2}$

69159.text: Two bodies A and B have moment of inertia $I_A$ and $I_B$, and angular momenta $L_A$ and $L_B$ respectively. Both of them have same kinetic energy of rotation. So the ratio $L_A$ to $L_B$ is
69159.sol:
The rotational kinetic energy of a body is given by $K = \dfrac{L^2}{2I}$, where $L$ is the angular momentum and $I$ is the moment of inertia.

Given that both bodies have the same rotational kinetic energy, $K_A = K_B$.

$\dfrac{L_A^2}{2I_A} = \dfrac{L_B^2}{2I_B}$

$\dfrac{L_A^2}{L_B^2} = \dfrac{I_A}{I_B}$

Taking the square root on both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_A}{I_B}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{I_A}{I_B}}$

69167.text: The power (P) is supplied to rotating body having moment of inertia 'I' and angular acceleration '$\alpha$'. Its instantaneous angular velocity is
69167.sol:
Power $P$ supplied to a rotating body is given by the product of torque $\tau$ and angular velocity $\omega$.

$P = \tau \omega$

The torque $\tau$ acting on the body is related to its moment of inertia $I$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$ by the relation:

$\tau = I \alpha$

Substituting the value of $\tau$ in the power equation:

$P = (I \alpha) \omega$

Rearranging for instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$:

$\omega = \dfrac{P}{I \alpha}$

Answer: $\dfrac{P}{I\alpha}$

70214.text: Three identical polaroids $P_1, P_2 and P_3$ are placed one after another. The pass axis of $P_2 and P_3$ are inclined at an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ with respect to axis of $P_1$. The source has an intensity $256 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^2$. The intensity of light at point ' $O$ ' is $\left(\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}=\sqrt{3} / 2, \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}=0 \cdot 5\right)$
70214.sol:
Given unpolarized initial intensity $I_0 = 256 \mathrm{ W}/\mathrm{m}^2$. After passing through the first polarizer $P_1$ at $0^{}^{\circ}$, the intensity reduces by half: $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2} = 128 \mathrm{ W}/\mathrm{m}^2$.

Light emerging from $P_1$ is polarized at $0^{}^{\circ}$ and encounters $P_2$ at $60^{}^{\circ}$.
By Malus's law, $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2(60^{}^{\circ}) = 128 \times (0.5)^2 = 32 \mathrm{ W}/\mathrm{m}^2$.

The polarization direction is now aligned with $P_2$'s axis at $60^{}^{\circ}$. Transmission through $P_3$ at $90^{}^{\circ}$ gives the final intensity:
$I_3 = I_2 \cos^2(30^{}^{\circ}) = 32 \times \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = 32 \times \frac{3}{4} = 24 \mathrm{ W}/\mathrm{m}^2$.

The intensity at point O is $24 \mathrm{ W}/\mathrm{m}^2$.

70451.text: A sonometer wire is vibrating in third overtone. There are
70451.sol:
A sonometer wire is fixed at both ends.

For a string fixed at both ends, the $p$-th overtone corresponds to the $(p+1)$-th harmonic.

The third overtone corresponds to the $4$-th harmonic.

In the $4$-th harmonic, the wire vibrates in $4$ loops.

Each loop contains one antinode, so the number of antinodes is $4$.

The number of nodes is one more than the number of loops, which is $4 + 1 = 5$.

Thus, there are $5$ nodes and $4$ antinodes.

Answer: 5 nodes and 4 antinodes

70521.subject: Physics
70521.text: A progressive wave of frequency 400 Hz is travelling with velocity $336 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. How far apart are the two points on a wave which are $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ out of phase?
70521.sol:
The wavelength is determined from the wave velocity and frequency using $v = f\lambda$.

Given $f = 400\,\text{Hz}$ and $v = 336\,\text{m/s}$, the wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{336}{400} = 0.84\,\text{m}$.

The phase difference $\Delta\phi$ and path difference $\Delta x$ are related by $\Delta\phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$.

A phase difference of $60^{}^{\circ}$ corresponds to $\Delta\phi = \frac{\pi}{3}\,\text{rad}$.

Solving for the path difference yields $\Delta x = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi}\Delta\phi = \frac{0.84}{2\pi} \cdot \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{0.84}{6} = 0.14\,\text{m}$.

70843.subject: Physics
70843.text: A point mass ' $m$ ' attached at one end of a massless, inextensible string of length ' $\ell$ ' performs a vertical circular motion and the string rotates in vertical plane, as shown in the diagram. The increase in the centripetal acceleration of the point mass when it moves from point $A$ to point C is [ $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity.]
70843.sol:
The centripetal acceleration at any point on the circular path of radius $\ell$ is given by $a_c = \frac{v^2}{\ell}$, where $v$ is the speed at that point.

Applying conservation of mechanical energy between point A (height $\ell$ above the reference level at C) and point C:

$\frac{1}{2}mv_A^2 + mg\ell = \frac{1}{2}mv_C^2$

Multiplying through by $\frac{2}{m}$ yields:

$v_A^2 + 2g\ell = v_C^2$

The increase in centripetal acceleration from A to C is:

$\Delta a_c = \frac{v_C^2}{\ell} - \frac{v_A^2}{\ell} = \frac{(v_A^2 + 2g\ell)}{\ell} - \frac{v_A^2}{\ell} = 2g$

Final Answer: $2g$

71011.subject: Biology
71011.text: Which one of the following parts of the pharynx is the continuation of the internal nares?
71011.sol:
The nasal cavity extends posteriorly and opens into the pharynx through the internal nares.

The pharynx is anatomically divided into three regions: the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and laryngopharynx.

The nasopharynx is the superior portion of the pharynx, located immediately posterior to the nasal cavity. It serves as the direct continuation of the internal nares and acts as a passageway for air.

The oropharynx lies posterior to the oral cavity, and the laryngopharynx is the inferior part, located posterior to the larynx.

The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that covers the glottis during swallowing to prevent food from entering the trachea.

Therefore, the nasopharynx is the part of the pharynx that is the continuation of the internal nares.

Answer: Nasopharynx.

(A) Pneumonia
(B) Emphysema
(C) Acute bronchitis
(D) Sinusitis

71133.sol:
Pneumonia is a respiratory disorder caused by bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.

Sinusitis is an inflammation of the sinuses that is often of bacterial origin.

Emphysema is a chronic, non-infectious disorder primarily caused by cigarette smoking.

Acute bronchitis is most commonly caused by viral infections rather than bacterial.

For respiratory infections like pneumonia and sinusitis, the use of a vapourizer is recommended to help loosen mucus and relieve congestion.

Therefore, pneumonia (A) and sinusitis (D) are the correct disorders.

Answer: A and D only

71441.subject: Biology
71441.text: In glycolysis, which enzyme requires $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ as cofactor?
71441.sol:
In the process of glycolysis, specific enzymes require metal ions or coenzymes as cofactors for their catalytic activity.

Hexokinase and Phosphofructokinase are kinase enzymes that catalyze the transfer of phosphate groups from ATP. They typically require $Mg^{2+}$ as a cofactor to stabilize the negative charges of ATP.

Glyceraldehyde phosphate dehydrogenase is an oxidoreductase enzyme that utilizes the coenzyme $NAD^+$ to catalyze its reaction and does not require a metal ion cofactor.

Aldolase, specifically Class II aldolase, is a metalloenzyme that requires a divalent metal ion such as $Zn^{2+}$ as a cofactor to stabilize the reaction intermediates during the cleavage of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate and dihydroxyacetone phosphate.

Thus, aldolase is the enzyme that requires $Zn^{2+}$ as a cofactor.

Answer: Aldolase

72134.subject: Physics
72134.text: The equivalent resistance of the following circuit is nearly
72134.sol:
The given circuit is a Wheatstone bridge.

Let us check the balance condition of the bridge:
$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{AD}} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{R_{BC}}{R_{DC}} = \dfrac{15}{30} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{AD}} = \dfrac{R_{BC}}{R_{DC}}$, the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

Therefore, no current flows through the $4\ \Omega$ resistor in the branch $BD$, and it can be removed from the circuit.

The circuit now consists of two parallel branches:
Upper branch resistance, $R_{upper} = 5\ \Omega + 15\ \Omega = 20\ \Omega$
Lower branch resistance, $R_{lower} = 10\ \Omega + 30\ \Omega = 40\ \Omega$

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ of the circuit is given by the parallel combination of $R_{upper}$ and $R_{lower}$:
$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R_{upper}} + \dfrac{1}{R_{lower}}$

$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{2 + 1}{40} = \dfrac{3}{40}\ \Omega^{-1}$

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{40}{3}\ \Omega \approx 13.3\ \Omega$

Answer: $13.3\ \Omega$

72186.subject: Physics
72186.text: A metal rod of length '$l$' rotates about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a magnetic field of induction 'B'. If the emf induced between the ends of the rod is 'e', then the number of revolutions made by the rod per second is
72186.sol:
The induced emf $e$ across the ends of a metal rod of length $l$ rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a perpendicular magnetic field $B$ is given by:

$e = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$

The angular velocity $\omega$ is related to the frequency $f$ (number of revolutions per second) by:

$\omega = 2 \pi f$

Substituting the value of $\omega$ in the expression for emf:

$e = \dfrac{1}{2} B (2 \pi f) l^2$

$e = B \pi f l^2$

Rearranging for $f$, we get:

$f = \dfrac{e}{B \pi l^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{e}{B\pi l^2}$

72266.subject: Physics
72266.text: A proton moves at a constant speed $v$ along the x-axis through a crossed electric and magnetic field. The magnetic field is $\vec{B} = B_0\hat{k}$ T. The electric field $\vec{E}$ in V/m is
72266.sol:
Velocity of the proton, $\vec{v} = v\hat{i}$

Magnetic field, $\vec{B} = B_0\hat{k}$

For the proton to move at a constant velocity, the net force acting on it must be zero.

Lorentz force, $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = 0$

$\vec{E} = -(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$

$\vec{E} = -(v\hat{i} \times B_0\hat{k})$

$\vec{E} = -vB_0(\hat{i} \times \hat{k})$

Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$

$\vec{E} = -vB_0(-\hat{j}) = vB_0\hat{j}$

Answer: $vB_0\hat{j}$

72474.subject: Physics
72474.text: A simple harmonic progressive wave is represented as $Y = 0.04 \sin\pi (2t - 0.02x)$ m. At a given instant of time, the phase difference between two particles 10 m apart is (in radian)
72474.sol:
The given equation of the wave is $Y = 0.04 \sin(\pi(2t - 0.02x))$.

The phase of the wave at position $x$ and time $t$ is $\phi = 2\pi t - 0.02\pi x$.

Comparing this with the standard wave equation $Y = A \sin(\omega t - kx)$, the propagation constant is $k = 0.02\pi$.

At a given instant of time, the phase difference $\Delta \phi$ between two particles separated by a distance $\Delta x$ is given by $\Delta \phi = k \Delta x$.

Given the distance between the particles is $\Delta x = 10$ m.

Substituting the values, we get $\Delta \phi = 0.02\pi (10) = 0.2\pi = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$ radian.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{5}$

77630.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = \sin[x]$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer function and $g(x) = |x|$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 0} \{f(x) g(x)\}$ equal to?
77630.sol:
Given $f(x) = \sin[x]$ and $g(x) = |x|$.

To find $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) g(x)$, we evaluate the left-hand limit (LHL) and the right-hand limit (RHL).

For LHL, as $x \to 0^{-}$, $[x] = -1$ and $|x| = -x$.

$\lim_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) g(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} (\sin(-1))(-x) = (-\sin 1)(0) = 0$

For RHL, as $x \to 0^{+}$, $[x] = 0$ and $|x| = x$.

$\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) g(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} (\sin 0)(x) = (0)(0) = 0$

Since LHL = RHL = $0$, the limit exists and is equal to $0$.

Answer: $0$

78045.text: Three dice are thrown. What is the probability that each face shows only multiples of 3 ?
78045.sol:
On throw of 3 dice,
Number of possible outcomes $=6^3=216$
Favourable outcomes
$\begin{aligned} &=\{(3,3,3),(3,3,6),(3,6,3),(6,3,3),(3,6,6) \\ &(6,3,6),(6,6,3),(6,6,6)\}\end{aligned}$
Probability $=\frac{\text{ Number of favourable outcomes }}{\text{ Number of total outcomes }}=\frac{8}{216}=\frac{1}{27}$

78765.subject: Mathematics
78765.text: If a line in 3 dimensions makes angles $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ with the positive directions of the coordinate axes, then what is $\cos(\alpha+\beta)\cos(\alpha-\beta)$ equal to?
78765.sol:
Using the trigonometric identity $\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B) = \cos^2 A - \sin^2 B$, we have:

$\cos(\alpha+\beta)\cos(\alpha-\beta) = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\beta$

Since $\sin^2\beta = 1 - \cos^2\beta$, the expression becomes:

$\cos^2\alpha - (1 - \cos^2\beta) = \cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta - 1$

For a line in three-dimensional space making angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ with the coordinate axes, the sum of the squares of its direction cosines is $1$:

$\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$

$\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta - 1 = -\cos^2\gamma$

Substituting this into the earlier expression, we get $-\cos^2\gamma$.

Answer: $-\cos^2\gamma$

78813.text:
Passage: The equation of the sphere $S$ is $x^2+y^2+z^2-4x-6y-12z+k=0$.

Question: What is the radius of the sphere passing through origin and concentric with the sphere $S$ ?
options: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
78813.sol:
The equation of the given sphere is $x^2+y^2+z^2-4x-6y-12z+k=0$.

The center of the sphere is $(2, 3, 6)$.

The required sphere is concentric with the given sphere, so its center is also $(2, 3, 6)$.

Since the required sphere passes through the origin $(0, 0, 0)$, its radius is the distance between the center and the origin.

$R = \sqrt{(2-0)^2 + (3-0)^2 + (6-0)^2}$

$R = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7$

Answer: $7$

$P\left(x \ge 3\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{2}\dfrac{1}{4} + \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{3}\dfrac{1}{4} + \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) +. \ldots$
$= \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}} = {\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{2}$
$P\left(\dfrac{x \ge 5}{x \ge 3}\right) = \dfrac{P\left[\left(x \ge 5\right) \cap \left(x \ge 3\right)\right]}{P\left(x \ge 3\right)} = \dfrac{P\left(x \ge 5\right)}{P\left(x \ge 3\right)} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{4}}{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{2}} = \dfrac{9}{16}$

Substituting $n = 2 \left(l + m\right)$ in $lm + mn + nl = 0,$ we get

Hence $m = - 2l ⇒ n = - 2l$ or $m = - \dfrac{l}{2}$⇒ n = l$

94138.text:
Two identical balls $A$ and $B$, each of mass$0. 1kg$, are attached to two identical massless springs. The spring-mass system is constrained to move inside a rigid smooth pipe bent in the form of a circle as shown in the figure. The pipe is fixed in a horizontal plane. 94138.sol:
Given, Mass of each block A and B, m = 0.1 kg

Radius of circle, $R = 0 . 06m$



The natural length of spring ${l}_{0} = \text{0.06} \pi = \pi \text{R}$~(Half circle) and spring constant,

$k = 0 . 1Nm^{- 1}$

In the stretched position elongation in each spring

$\text{x} = \text{R} \theta$

Let us draw FBD of A



Spring in lower side is stretched by 2x and on upper side compressed by 2x. Therefore, a force 2kx on each block would be exerted by each spring.

Hence, a restoring force, F = 4kx will act on A in the direction shown in figure.

Restoring torque of this force about origin

$τ = - \text{F. R} = - \left(4 \text{kx}\right) \text{R} = - \left(4 \text{kR} \theta\right) \text{R}$

or~$τ = - 4 {kR}^{2} \cdot \theta$ ..... (i)

Since, $τ ∝ - \theta$, each ball executes angular SHM about origin O.

Equation. (i) can be written as

$\text{I} \alpha = - 4 {kR}^{2} \theta$

or $\left({mR}^{2}\right) \alpha = - 4 {kR}^{2} \theta$

or $\alpha = - \left(\dfrac{4 \text{k}}{\text{m}}\right) \theta$

Frequency of oscillation, $\text{f} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left|\dfrac{\text{acceleration}}{\text{displacement}}\right|}$

~ & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & $= \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left|\dfrac{\alpha}{\theta}\right|}$

~ & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & $\text{f} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \text{k}}{\text{m}}}$

Substituting the values, we have

$\text{f} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times \text{0.1}}{\text{0.1}}} = \dfrac{1}{\pi} \text{Hz}$

97076.subject: Botany
97076.text: In a unilocular ovary with a single ovule, the placentation is
97076.sol:
Placentation is the arrangement of the ovules in the ovary and their attachment to it. Placentation are of various type in the angiosperms - marginal, axile, central, parietal, basal, and free central.

In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary without any locules. Pea plant has this arrangement. When the ovules are attached to the central column and the ovary wall forms chambers called locules separating the ovules from each other is said the axile placentation. In parietal, the ovules are attached to the inner wall or towards the periphery of the ovary. In basal placentation the ovules are attached at the base of the ovary with single locus or chamber. Free-central placentation is when the ovules are attached at the central axis of the ovary without any septa present like in axile pattern.

100114.subject: Physics
100114.text: The mechanical power $P$ delivered to a particle depends on time $t$ and position $x$ according to the equation $P = \dfrac{\alpha - t^2}{\beta x}$. The dimensions of the product $(\alpha \times \beta)$ are:
100114.sol:
According to the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, quantities added or subtracted must have the same dimensions.

From the numerator $(\alpha - t^2)$, we have:
$[\alpha] = [t^2] = [\mathrm{T}^2]$

The dimensional formula for power $P$ is $[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-3}]$.

Substituting the dimensions into the given equation $P = \dfrac{\alpha - t^2}{\beta x}$:
$[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-3}] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{T}^2]}{[\beta] [\mathrm{L}]}$

Rearranging for $[\beta]$:
$[\beta] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{T}^2]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-3}] [\mathrm{L}]} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{T}^2]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-3}]} = [\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-3} \mathrm{~T}^5]$

The dimensions of the product $(\alpha \times \beta)$ are:
$[\alpha \times \beta] = [\mathrm{T}^2] \times [\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-3} \mathrm{~T}^5] = [\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-3} \mathrm{~T}^7]$

Answer: $[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-3} \mathrm{~T}^7]$

100520.subject: Physics
100520.text: A bullet fired horizontally into a thick wooden block undergoes uniform deceleration. It takes $0.1\text{ s}$ to travel through the first $30\text{ cm}$ of the block, and its velocity at the end of this $30\text{ cm}$ is exactly half of its entry velocity. What is the entry velocity of the bullet?
100520.sol:
Let the entry velocity of the bullet be $u$ and the final velocity after travelling $30\text{ cm}$ be $v$.

Given:
Distance $s = 30\text{ cm} = 0.3\text{ m}$
Time $t = 0.1\text{ s}$
Final velocity $v = \dfrac{u}{2}$

For uniformly accelerated (or decelerated) motion, the displacement can be expressed in terms of average velocity:
$s = \left(\dfrac{u + v}{2}\right)t$

Substituting the given values:
$0.3 = \left(\dfrac{u + \dfrac{u}{2}}{2}\right) \times 0.1$

$0.3 = \left(\dfrac{3u}{4}\right) \times 0.1$

$3 = \dfrac{3u}{4}$

$u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$

The entry velocity of the bullet is $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$

101811.sol:
Statement A: Peltier coefficient is numerically equal to the potential difference across the junctions of the thermocouple through which current is flowing.

102890.subject: Physics
102890.text:
Read the following statements regarding equipotential surfaces:
(A) For a uniform electric field, the equipotential surfaces are concentric spheres.
(B) Two equipotential surfaces can never intersect each other.
(C) The electric field is always tangential to the equipotential surface.
(D) The work done in moving a test charge between any two points on an equipotential surface is zero.

How many of the above statements are correct?
102890.sol:
Statement (A) is incorrect because for a uniform electric field, the equipotential surfaces are parallel planes, not concentric spheres.

Statement (B) is correct because if two equipotential surfaces intersect, there would be two different values of electric potential at the point of intersection, which is impossible.

Statement (C) is incorrect because the electric field is always perpendicular (normal), not tangential, to the equipotential surface.

Statement (D) is correct because the potential difference between any two points on an equipotential surface is zero ($\Delta V = 0$), so the work done $W = q\Delta V = 0$.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (B) and (D), are correct.

Answer: Two

103677.subject: Physics
103677.text: A long straight solid cylindrical wire of radius $a$ carries a steady uniform current $I$. The magnitude of the magnetic field is maximum at the surface of the wire. At which of the following pairs of radial distances from the axis of the wire is the magnitude of the magnetic field exactly one-third of its maximum value?
103677.sol:
The magnetic field due to a long straight solid cylindrical wire of radius $a$ carrying a steady uniform current $I$ is maximum at its surface ($r = a$).

Maximum magnetic field, $B_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$

Inside the wire ($r < a$), the magnetic field is given by:
$B_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2} = B_{\text{max}} \left(\dfrac{r}{a}\right)$

We are given that $B_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{B_{\text{max}}}{3}$.
$\Rightarrow B_{\text{max}} \left(\dfrac{r}{a}\right) = \dfrac{B_{\text{max}}}{3}$
$\Rightarrow r = \dfrac{a}{3}$

Outside the wire ($r > a$), the magnetic field is given by:
$B_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = B_{\text{max}} \left(\dfrac{a}{r}\right)$

We are given that $B_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{B_{\text{max}}}{3}$.
$\Rightarrow B_{\text{max}} \left(\dfrac{a}{r}\right) = \dfrac{B_{\text{max}}}{3}$
$\Rightarrow r = 3a$

Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic field is one-third of its maximum value at radial distances of $\dfrac{a}{3}$ and $3a$.

Answer: $\dfrac{a}{3}$ and $3a$

105560.subject: Physics
105560.text: For ideal light emitting diodes (LEDs) fabricated from various semiconductor materials, a graph is plotted with the wavelength of the emitted light ($\lambda$) on the y-axis and the reciprocal of the bandgap energy ($\dfrac{1}{E_g}$) on the x-axis, where $E_g$ is measured in Joules. What will be the shape of this graph and the value of its slope?
options: Straight line passing through the origin with slope $\dfrac{h}{c}$
Straight line passing through the origin with slope $\dfrac{hc}{e}$
Straight line passing through the origin with slope $hc$
105560.sol:
The energy of the emitted photon is approximately equal to the bandgap energy of the semiconductor, given by the relation:
$E_g = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

Rearranging this equation to express wavelength as a function of the reciprocal of the bandgap energy gives:
$\lambda = hc \left(\dfrac{1}{E_g}\right)$

Comparing this with the standard equation of a straight line passing through the origin, $y = mx$, we identify:
$y = \lambda$
$x = \dfrac{1}{E_g}$

Therefore, the graph of $\lambda$ versus $\dfrac{1}{E_g}$ is a straight line passing through the origin. The slope of this line ($m$) corresponds to the product of Planck's constant and the speed of light ($hc$).

Answer: Straight line passing through the origin with slope $hc$

108672.subject: Chemistry
108672.text:
The standard enthalpies of formation for three hypothetical solid salts (P, Q, and R) and their respective aqueous ions are given in the table below (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$):

Salt$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Solid})$$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Cation}(aq))$$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Anion}(aq))$
P-900-400-400
Q-500-300-250
R-700-350-360

What is the correct order of these salts from the most exothermic to the most endothermic standard enthalpy of solution?
108672.sol:
The standard enthalpy of solution ($\Delta H_{sol}^\circ$) for a salt is calculated using Hess's Law:
$\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Cation}(aq)) + \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Anion}(aq)) - \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Solid})$

Calculating for each salt:
For P: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-400) + (-400) - (-900) = -800 + 900 = +100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
For Q: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-300) + (-250) - (-500) = -550 + 500 = -50 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
For R: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-350) + (-360) - (-700) = -710 + 700 = -10 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

111926.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Pairs of compounds)List-II (Type of isomerism)
(A) Diethylamine and Methyl propylamine(I) Chain isomerism
(B) Bu\tan^{-1}-ol and Butan-2-ol(II) Position isomerism
(C) Pentane and Isopentane(III) Functional isomerism
(D) Propanone and Propanal(IV) Metamerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
111926.sol:
(A) Diethylamine ($CH_3CH_2-NH-CH_2CH_3$) and Methyl propylamine ($CH_3-NH-CH_2CH_2CH_3$) have different alkyl groups attached to the polyvalent -NH- group. They exhibit metamerism. (A $\rightarrow$ IV)

(B) Bu\tan^{-1}-ol and Butan-2-ol differ only in the position of the -OH group on the main carbon chain. They exhibit position isomerism. (B $\rightarrow$ II)

(C) Pentane (a straight chain) and Isopentane (a branched chain) differ in their carbon skeletons. They exhibit chain isomerism. (C $\rightarrow$ I)

(D) Propanone is a ketone and Propanal is an aldehyde. Since they have different functional groups but the same molecular formula ($C_3H_6O$), they exhibit functional isomerism. (D $\rightarrow$ III)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

119278.text:
Match the carbonyl compounds in List I with their corresponding aldol addition products in List II.

List IList II
(A) Ethanal(I) 3-Hydroxy-2-methylpentanal
(B) Propanone(II) 4-Hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one
(C) Propanal(III) 2-Ethyl-3-hydroxyhexanal
(D) Butanal(IV) 3-Hydroxybutanal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
119278.sol:
Aldol addition occurs when aldehydes or ketones with $\alpha$-hydrogens are treated with a dilute base.

For Ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$), the self-addition product is 3-hydroxybutanal.

For Propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$), the self-addition product is 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one.

For Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$), the $\alpha$-carbon of one molecule attacks the carbonyl carbon of another, forming 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal.

For Butanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$), following the same mechanism, the product is 2-ethyl-3-hydroxyhexanal.

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

Reason (R): In $\text{C}_4$ plants, RuBisCO is located in bundle sheath cells where the continuous decarboxylation of malic acid maintains a high intracellular concentration of $\text{CO}_2$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
125660.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because $\text{C}_4$ plants have a mechanism that increases the concentration of $\text{CO}_2$ at the enzyme site, which prevents RuBisCO from acting as an oxygenase. This lack of photorespiration minimizes carbon loss and leads to higher productivity.

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the assertion. In $\text{C}_4$ plants, the initial carbon fixation occurs in mesophyll cells to form a $\text{C}_4$ acid such as malic acid. This acid is transported to the bundle sheath cells, where it is decarboxylated. The continuous release of $\text{CO}_2$ in the bundle sheath cells, where RuBisCO is localized, maintains a high intracellular $\text{CO}_2$ concentration. This high $\text{CO}_2/\text{O}_2$ ratio ensures that RuBisCO functions primarily as a carboxylase, thereby avoiding photorespiration.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

127209.text: What can nations endowed with rich biodiversity expect to reap?
127209.sol: The narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are obvious; humans derive countless direct economic benefits from naturefood (cereals, pulses, fruits), firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products (tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins, perfumes ) and products of medicinal importance. More than 25 per cent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants and 25,000 species of plants contribute to the traditional medicines used by native peoples around the world. Nobody knows how many more medicinally useful plants there are in tropical rain forests waiting to be explored. 127405.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the Amazonian rain forest, the number of fish species is greater than the number of bird species.

Reason (R): Tropical environments, unlike temperate ones, are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable, which promotes niche specialisation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
127405.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: According to the biodiversity data of the Amazonian rain forest, there are $3,000$ species of fishes and $1,300$ species of birds. Hence, fish species outnumber bird species.

Reason (R) is true: Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable compared to temperate regions. This constancy promotes niche specialisation and leads to greater species diversity.

However, Reason (R) explains the overall high biodiversity in tropical latitudes, but it does not specifically explain why the number of fish species is greater than the number of bird species in the Amazon. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

129725.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mammals have the ability to produce a concentrated urine.

Reason (R): The counter current mechanism maintains an increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium, which facilitates water reabsorption from the collecting duct.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
129725.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because mammals, including humans, can produce urine that is significantly more concentrated than the initial filtrate.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A). The counter current mechanism operating between the two limbs of the Henle's loop and the vasa recta maintains an increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium. This gradient is essential because it allows the passive reabsorption of water from the collecting duct, thereby concentrating the filtrate and producing hypertonic urine.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

130944.subject: Zoology
130944.text: What triggers the release of oxytocin during parturition?
130944.sol: The average duration of human pregnancy is about 9 months which is called the gestation period. Vigorous contraction of the uterus at the end of pregnancy causes expulsion/delivery of the foetus. This process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition. Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex. This triggers release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary. Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions, which in turn stimulates further secretion of oxytocin. The stimulatory reflex between the uterine contraction and oxytocin secretion continues resulting in stronger and stronger contractions. This leads to expulsion of the baby out of the uterus through the birth canal – parturition. Soon after the infant is delivered, the placenta is also expelled out of the uterus.
130944.meta: What triggers the release of oxytocin during parturition?

131445.subject: Zoology
131445.text: Who conducted the series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae that led to the discovery of the transforming principle?
131445.sol: In 1928, Frederick Griffith, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia), witnessed a miraculous transformation in the bacteria. During the course of his experiment, a living organism (bacteria) had changed in physical form. When Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) bacteria are grown on a culture plate, some produce smooth shiny colonies (S) while others produce rough colonies (R). This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, while R strain does not. Mice infected with the S strain (virulent) die from pneumonia infection but mice infected with the R strain do not develop pneumonia. Griffith was able to kill bacteria by heating them. He observed that heat-killed S strain bacteria injected into mice did not kill them. When he injected a mixture of heat-killed S and live R bacteria, the mice died. Moreover, he recovered living S bacteria from the dead mice. He concluded that the R strain bacteria had somehow been transformed by the heat-killed S strain bacteria. Some ‘transforming principle’, transferred from the heat-killed S strain, had enabled the R strain to synthesize a smooth polysaccharide coat and become virulent.
131445.meta: Who conducted the series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae that led to the discovery of the transforming principle?

131576.subject: Zoology
131576.text: What is the purpose of the operator and repressor in the lac operon?
options: To bind to the promoter region
To repress the expression of beta-galactosidase
131576.sol: In prokaryotes, control of the rate of transcriptional initiation is the predominant site for control of gene expression. In a transcription unit, the activity of RNA polymerase at a given promoter is in turn regulated by interaction with accessory proteins, which affect its ability to recognise start sites. These regulatory proteins can act both positively (activators) and negatively (repressors). The accessibility of promoter regions of prokaryotic DNA is in many cases regulated by the interaction of proteins with sequences termed operators. The operator region is adjacent to the promoter elements in most operons and in most cases the sequences of the operator bind a repressor protein. Each operon has its specific operator and specific repressor. For example, lac operator is present only in the lac operon and it interacts specifically with lac repressor only

131620.subject: Zoology
131620.text: What is the basis of variability/polymorphism in DNA sequences?
options: Accumulation of mutations in non-coding DNA sequences
131620.sol: Allelic (again recall the definition of alleles from Chapter 4) sequence variation has traditionally been described as a DNA polymorphism if more than one variant (allele) at a locus occurs in human population with a frequency greater than 0.01. In simple terms, if an inheritable mutation is observed in a population at high frequency, it is referred to as DNA polymorphism. The probability of such variation to be observed in noncoding DNA sequences would be higher as mutations in these sequences may not have any immediate effect/impact on an individual’s reproductive ability. These mutations keep on accumulating generation after generation, and form one of the basis of variability/polymorphism.
